assigned.title: A player that can actually be operated
assigned.acceptance: The player has controls. TODAY IT HAS NONE: player-surface.tsx sets the native controls attribute on a video element and renders a debug panel, and its own header says 'NO CONTROLS ARE BUILT HERE'. There is no play, pause, seek, volume, fullscreen, subtitle, audio, quality or source control anywhere in this product. REQUIRED: play/pause, a seek bar with buffered ranges, volume and mute, fullscreen, a subtitle menu and an audio-track menu driven by PW-0206, and a source/quality state the viewer can read. REQUIRED: keyboard operation -- space, arrows, F, M, and Escape -- because there is not one keyboard handler in the entire application today and a Windows media application that cannot be driven from the keyboard is not finished. REQUIRED: an idle-hide overlay that never hides a control from a keyboard or screen-reader user. REQUIRED: the controls layer sends no side effect the state machine does not already own; playback-effects.ts deliberately exposes four effects and its header says FOUR, AND NO MORE, so a control that needs a fifth is a machine change with its own justification. REQUIRED: the controls read the adapter, not Shaka, so the same UI operates the native engine.
assigned.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. 

ROUND 108 SURFACE AMENDMENT, recorded as task.definition_changed before any write. The adapter boundary and the Shaka adapter join the write surface -- four named files, all previously PW-0206's and now unowned -- because two acceptance clauses are unreachable without them: PlayerAdapter cannot report BUFFERED RANGES at all, and it cannot report TRACKS unless it performed the load, which it did not and must not. Routing the load through the adapter was rejected on a RIGHTS ground: PlayerSession candidates carry protection and compatibility, the client PlaybackSession carries neither, and projecting one into the other would mean inventing a rights-bearing fact. That reconciliation is PW-0203's by the round-82 ruling and was not taken. Instead the boundary gains two READS -- resynchronise(), which the boundary already anticipated (the resynchronised event exists and PW-0204 requires mpv to resynchronise from properties on queue overflow) and getBufferedRanges(), beside the three pull-side reads already there. player-adapter.ts moved from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths; it was already inside the reviewed surface, so this widens the write surface and not the fingerprint. The e2e gate needed a path: e2e/tests/player-controls.spec.ts was added to the surface in the same round, one new file, because vitest here runs with environment "node" and a keyboard clause cannot be evidenced without a keyboard.

typecheck.evidence: npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json: clean. npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. npm run lint: 12 tasks, 0 errors; the single warning is a pre-existing unused import in apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts, not on this surface. e2e/ typechecks clean too, which matters because the keyboard and overlay clauses are evidenced there.

unit.evidence:
npm run test: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. apps/web 1597 tests passed, up from 1534 -- 63 new, 0 failed. The player directory alone is 397 tests across 22 files, up from 336.

HOW THE WORK IS SPLIT, BECAUSE apps/web HAS NO DOM. vitest.config.ts sets environment "node", so no effect runs, no keystroke is dispatched and no menu opens. The same observation PW-0307 made one task earlier, used the same way:
  - controls/controls-state.ts holds every DECISION a viewer can feel -- how far a key seeks, when the bar may dim, what a track is called, what a source line says -- as pure functions. 42 tests.
  - controls/player-controls.test.tsx renders with renderToStaticMarkup and asserts the MARKUP a browser receives before hydration, which is where every accessibility promise that lives in an attribute can be checked. 14 tests.
  - e2e/tests/player-controls.spec.ts is the keyboard and the menus, in a real browser. 10 tests, recorded under the e2e gate.

WHAT I ADDED THIS ROUND ON TOP OF THE IMPLEMENTATION ALREADY IN THE TREE, and it is the clause that was missing rather than a polish pass.

PW-0206 WAS STILL UNREACHABLE. Its module -- the normalised vocabulary, the identity, reapply, rememberChoice -- was imported by NOTHING. PL-0716's readiness audit had to score track selection PARTIAL for exactly that reason, and this task's acceptance asks for menus "driven by PW-0206". The menus were driven by this task's own trackOptions; the POLICY was not wired at all, so a viewer's choice did not survive a candidate switch -- which is the one clause PW-0206 exists for.
  - controls-state.ts gains restoreCommands() and rememberFromMenu(), pure, which call PW-0206's reapply/rememberChoice. 11 new tests.
  - player-controls.tsx remembers a TrackIdentity on every menu selection and, when a `tracks` event arrives, issues only the commands restoreCommands returns.
  - MUTATION-TESTED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, four plausible wrong implementations, each reverted: remembering the track id instead of the identity (3 failed); dropping the already-selected guard, which would re-command on every candidate switch forever (1); treating a subtitle "off" as "no choice", which would let a default-marked track on the next candidate turn text back on for a viewer who switched it off (2); and a guard written as "restored differs from current" instead of "restored exists and differs from current" (SURVIVED the first four tests -- it only misbehaves when the viewer's language is absent AND another audio track is already selected, where it would command selectAudioTrack(null), which the adapter throws on. A test was added for exactly that case and the mutant now fails).

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SHORTCUT. resolveTracks -- the DEFAULT selection for a viewer who has chosen nothing -- needs a PlaybackCapabilities, and this layer does not have one and must not invent one. watch-session.ts refuses the same thing in its own words: a capability union assembled by something that cannot see the engines "would be a capability claim nobody measured". Routing a real profile down here is PW-0308's settings work and PL-0502's engine union. Until then the engine's own default plays and the viewer's explicit choice is honoured, which is the honest subset and is stated in the module rather than left to be discovered.

ONE DEFECT FIXED IN THE INHERITED CODE: OverlayInput.pointerIsCoarse was documented as "the viewer has asked the operating system to reduce motion", which it has never been and which overlayVisibility has never read. Corrected in place with a note, because a comment that describes the wrong input is worse than none -- the next person to add a rule would have reasoned from it.

e2e.evidence:
RE-RECORDED, AND THE REASON IS A HOLE IN THE PREVIOUS RECORDING RATHER THAN AN ADDITION TO IT.

THE PREVIOUS e2e GATE REPORTED A DEVELOPMENT-MODE RUN AND DID NOT SAY THAT PRODUCTION WAS UNRUN. It was. Running the full suite in production mode against a real PostgreSQL, which PL-0715's work required anyway, ALL TEN player-controls cases failed at `toHaveCount(1)` on the control bar.

NOT A DEFECT IN THE BAR. On that build /watch answers with a refusal rather than a session -- observed heading "Sign in to watch this", because the harness's browser context is anonymous and authentication refuses before the catalog is consulted -- so there is no player, and a bar that had rendered anyway would have been the row of buttons wired to nothing that player-surface.tsx renders conditionally to prevent. The ten cases were simply written as though development were the only configuration.

THE REPAIR, WHICH FOLLOWS THE RULE PW-0601 AND docs/TEST_MATRIX.md ALREADY STATE -- a row that does not run says why BY NAME. The ten operation cases stand down when CATALOG_AVAILABILITY is "refused", through a single guard inside the shared openPlayer helper so the reason cannot drift between them, and the reason names what was actually observed. An ELEVENTH case runs in their place in exactly that configuration and asserts what is true there: the route answers 200, it renders a visible non-empty refusal heading, and NO CONTROL BAR PRETENDS OTHERWISE.

TWO DRAFTS OF THAT ELEVENTH CASE WERE WRONG AND A PRODUCTION RUN CORRECTED BOTH -- recorded because the second is the interesting one. It first asserted an h1; PlaybackUnavailable renders an h2, the route frame owning the h1. It then asserted the heading matched /playback|play/, and the heading it met was "Sign in to watch this" -- authentication refusing before the catalog. WHICH refusal is therefore deliberately not pinned: there are four, the one reached depends on configuration this case does not control, and pinning one would make a test about the player fail the next time a deployment's reason changed.

THE RUNS, BOTH MODES, AFTER EVERY CHANGE THIS ROUND.
  development, full chromium+api suite: 103 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed.
  production + real PostgreSQL 16, cold database, --workers=4, full chromium+api suite: 77 passed, 41 skipped, 0 failed. The ten operation cases are among the skips, each naming its reason; the eleventh passes.

THE TEN CASES THEMSELVES ARE UNCHANGED and still cover what they covered: every named control present with an accessible name, the native video chrome gone, the whole bar reachable by TAB in order, SPACE operating the player without scrolling the page, the arrows on volume rather than the page, M mutes and the button says which state it is in, a track menu that opens and announces itself and admits an empty source, ESCAPE closing it, THE BAR NEVER LEAVING THE ACCESSIBILITY TREE however it is dimmed, and the seek bar announcing a TIME rather than a percentage.

STILL NOT ASSERTED, AND THE REASON STILL MATTERS MORE THAN THE OMISSION: that the picture moves, because no real media decodes in this harness; and the re-application of a viewer's track choice across a real candidate switch end to end, because no harness here produces two candidates with real track lists. The decision behind that one has 11 unit tests and four caught mutations; the three lines that issue it are unverified wiring and are named as such.

AND A GAP THIS EXPOSED THAT BELONGS TO NOBODY YET: operating the player on a DEPLOYMENT needs both a configured catalog source and a signed-in viewer, and no spec owns that journey. It is named in the skip reason rather than left for the next person to rediscover.
